props.text: All-on-4 Dental Implants in Alexandria, VA

At 2855 Duke Street, Dr. Esam Nahlah replaces a failing or missing arch with a fixed bridge on four implants. The rear two are angled into denser bone, so bone loss often does not rule you out, and most patients go home with provisional teeth.
A fixed provisional, in most cases
The rooms behind your new arch.
An arch you never take out.
A denture sits on the gum and shifts when you eat. An All-on-4 arch is screwed onto implants, so it stays put, and the implants keep loading the jaw.
Stays in when you eat, talk and sleep
No adhesive, and no rubbing on the gums
The jawbone keeps a load, which slows its loss
Brushed and flossed in place, like teeth
Fewer relines and repairs over the years
Your All-on-4 in Alexandria, visit by visit.
Dr. Nahlah examines you and takes a cone-beam scan, then goes through candidacy, cost and timing with you.
Under local anesthetic with nitrous oxide or oral sedation, the four implants are placed and, in most cases, your provisional teeth are fitted the same visit.
Over three to four months the implants fuse, and short reviews check integration and adjust the provisional teeth.
The definitive zirconia arch is fitted. From then on it is cleaned like natural teeth, with a professional cleaning every six months.
Upper and lower on implants · case 33
Upper and lower on implants · case 27
What does All-on-4 cost in Alexandria?

Your price is set after the scan, once it is clear whether one or both arches need restoring and whether any grafting comes first. Most PPO plans are accepted with claims filed for you, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
What if I have bone loss?
Bone loss is often why All-on-4 is chosen: tilting the rear implants reaches bone that straight ones would miss. Some mouths still need grafting first, and the scan shows which.
How long until the final teeth?
About three to four months after surgery, and then the gum takes another two to four months to settle around the zirconia arch.
Which number should Alexandria patients call?
(571) 617-7245 if you are new to the practice, and (703) 940-5410 if you are already a patient.
Is All-on-4 done the same way in McLean?
Yes. The same specialist and the same team work at both offices, each with a laboratory in the building.

props.text: All-on-4 Dental Implants in McLean, VA

Four implants carry a whole upper or lower arch, and in most cases you leave the McLean office the same day with fixed provisional teeth. Dr. Esam Nahlah plans the arch on a cone-beam scan and places it at Suite 220, 7901 Jones Branch Drive.
Three things every All-on-4 patient gets.
A working provisional arch, screwed in place before you leave. Nobody goes home without teeth.
Five years on the implant work, conditional on Precare: a cleaning every six months, the interval any set of teeth needs.
Already holding an All-on-4 quote from somewhere else? Bring it and the scan; reviewing it here costs nothing.
How an arch comes together in McLean.
Cone-beam imaging of the jaw shows whether four implants will hold, or whether grafting is needed first. Price, insurance and financing are on the table at this visit.
Teeth that cannot be saved come out, where the case allows on the same day the implants go in, by the same specialist.
Four implants go in through a printed guide, the back two tilted toward denser bone, and the provisional arch is fitted before you go home.
Three to four months on, the final zirconia arch replaces the provisional, and the gum keeps healing around it for two to four months more.
Each case shows both jaws restored, before and after.
How much does All-on-4 cost in McLean?

It depends on whether one arch or both are restored, whether grafting is needed, and the material of the final arch: a zirconia arch is not the same object as an acrylic one. Your figure is set at the consultation, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
Can both arches be done at once?
Yes: upper, lower or both. When both are restored, the practice calls the case a double arch.
Will I have teeth when I leave the office?
In most cases, yes: a fixed provisional arch goes in on implant day and stays while the implants integrate.
What sedation is offered for All-on-4 in McLean?
Nitrous oxide or oral sedation, given by the practice's own team; IV sedation is not offered. Plan a ride both ways after oral sedation.
Suite 220 at 7901 Jones Branch Drive, on the second floor with parking underneath, and the closer office for McLean, Vienna, Great Falls and Reston.

The only replacement that works like a root.
A post in the jawbone takes the load a tooth root used to carry. Nothing else does that: a denture rests on the gum, and a conventional bridge leans on the teeth either side of the gap.
Healthy neighboring teeth are left alone

Extractions, gum treatment or bone grafting where the scan shows a need, so the implant has sound bone to fuse with.

What do dental implants cost in Alexandria?

Your price comes from your own scan: how many teeth, how long they have been missing, the materials, and whether bone or gum needs treatment first. It is laid out at the consultation along with insurance and financing, and claims are filed for you.
Which number do I call to book?
New patients call (571) 617-7245; current patients call (703) 940-5410.
Is it the same specialist as in McLean?
Yes. Dr. Esam Nahlah sees implant patients at both offices, with the same team and a laboratory in each building.
It is done with sedation, so you stay relaxed and feel no pain during it. Afterwards most people manage with over-the-counter medication and are back to normal within about a week.
What if I have lost bone?
Many patients qualify after bone grafting or extractions. Grafting is its own procedure, with several months of healing before the implant goes in.
How do I care for an implant?
Like a natural tooth: brush twice a day, floss once, and keep the six-month cleanings, which also keep the five-year warranty.

Dr. Esam Nahlah plans, places and restores dental implants at his Tysons Corner office, Suite 220 at 7901 Jones Branch Drive in McLean: a single tooth, a bridge or a whole arch, made in the lab in the same building.

Where the implant goes is decided on a screen first.
At the Tysons Corner office every implant starts as a cone-beam scan: the jaw in three dimensions, with bone volume and nerve position measured before surgery rather than discovered during it.
The scan becomes a printed guide, so the implant lands at the planned angle and depth, with smaller incisions and a shorter recovery.

Time with Dr. Nahlah, a cone-beam scan and an examination. You leave knowing whether you are a candidate, what it costs and how long it will take.

How much do dental implants cost in McLean?

It is set at your consultation in Tysons Corner, once the scan shows how many implants you need, whether bone has to be rebuilt first and what goes on top. Most PPO plans are accepted with claims filed for you, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
Where do I go for my implant appointments?
Suite 220 at 7901 Jones Branch Drive, McLean, on the second floor, with parking underneath the building.
Does Dr. Nahlah place the implants himself?

props.text: Prosthodontist vs Periodontist vs General Dentist

A prosthodontist is a dentist who has trained for three more years in replacing and restoring teeth: implants, crowns, bridges, veneers and dentures. Here is how that differs from a general dentist and from a periodontist, and when it matters.
A prosthodontist rebuilds what is missing or broken.
Prosthodontics is one of the dental specialties recognized by the American Dental Association. Its work is

: dental implants, crowns, bridges, veneers, complete and partial dentures, and full-mouth rehabilitation. After dental school a prosthodontist trains for three more years in exactly this work, including the laboratory side of making it.
Dr. Esam Nahlah is board-certified by the American Board of Prosthodontics, a Diplomate since 2013, and a
Fellow of the American College of Prosthodontists
. He also teaches residents in the prosthodontics program at Virginia Commonwealth University, dentists in training to become prosthodontists.
Three kinds of dentist a patient with missing or failing teeth may meet, and what each one is trained for.
Your first call for most dental care.
A dentist who looks after everyday care for the whole family, and refers to a specialist when a case needs one.
The specialist in the gums and the bone around teeth.
Treats the tissues that hold teeth, and implants, in place: gum disease above all, and often implant placement.
Gum disease, from bleeding gums to advanced loss
The crown or arch on an implant often comes from another dentist
The specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.
Plans the finished teeth first, then works back to the implants, crowns or dentures that build them.
Trained in the laboratory work behind the teeth
Three years of specialty training after dental school
When a prosthodontist is worth seeing.
A general dentist handles most care well. These are the cases where the specialty earns its keep.
Implants, bridges or a full arch, planned from the finished teeth backwards, so the implants land where the teeth need them.
Dentures that will not stay put
A loose denture usually means receding bone. The fix is anchorage on implants, which a prosthodontist plans and restores.
A complex plan, or a second opinion
If another dentist called your case too complex, or quoted for implant surgery elsewhere, bring the plan and the scan: a second opinion here costs nothing.
What is the difference between a prosthodontist and a periodontist?

A periodontist specializes in the gums and the bone that hold teeth, treating gum disease and often placing implants. A prosthodontist specializes in replacing and restoring the teeth themselves. At this practice the prosthodontist plans and places the implants and makes the teeth on them.
Is a prosthodontist better than a general dentist?

For everyday care, a general dentist is the right first call. For missing teeth, implants, dentures and full-mouth work, a prosthodontist has three more years of training in exactly that, which is why general dentists refer those cases to one.
Do I need a referral to see a prosthodontist?
You can book a consultation with Dr. Nahlah directly. Dentists who want to refer a patient can do so through the practice's referral page.
What does board-certified mean for a prosthodontist?
That the prosthodontist has passed the examinations of the American Board of Prosthodontics and is a Diplomate of the Board. Dr. Nahlah became a Diplomate in 2013.
Many do. Dr. Nahlah plans, places and restores implants himself, so the surgery is planned around the teeth that go on top.
Where does Dr. Nahlah see patients?
At two offices: Suite 220, 7901 Jones Branch Drive in McLean, near Tysons Corner, and 2855 Duke Street in Alexandria.

props.text: Full-Mouth Reconstruction in McLean & Alexandria, VA

When teeth are worn, broken, failing or missing across the mouth, a prosthodontist rebuilds them together, with implants, crowns, bridges and veneers chosen to fit one design and one bite. Board-certified prosthodontist Dr. Esam Nahlah plans it and restores it.
Upper and lower designed to meet
Plans the surgery and the teeth
Not a list of treatments. One mouth, rebuilt as a system.
Full-mouth reconstruction, which prosthodontists also call full-mouth rehabilitation, restores most or all of the teeth in both jaws. Rather than fixing one tooth at a time, the specialist plans
: how the teeth look, how the upper and lower meet, and what each tooth needs to get there.
When one tooth at a time stops working.

Worn and broken teeth, several missing teeth, gum disease and a bite that no longer meets evenly tend to arrive together, and they are often one problem: once a tooth is lost, the bone under it deteriorates and the damage spreads to its neighbors.
Because a prosthodontist reads the whole mouth as one system, the question at your first visit is not
which tooth do I fix first
what does the finished mouth need
. A second opinion on a plan you already have costs nothing.
What a reconstruction can be built from.
Most plans combine several of these; the design decides which tooth gets which.
Custom caps over natural teeth that are too worn, cracked or stained for anything thinner.
Linked crowns that fill a gap. Carried on implants, a zirconia bridge leaves the healthy teeth beside it untouched.
Hand-designed porcelain over less than a millimeter of enamel, for front teeth that are chipped, spaced or stained.
Where teeth are missing or beyond saving, implants carry the new teeth, from a single crown to a fixed zirconia arch.
How a reconstruction is planned and built.
Time with Dr. Nahlah, your goals, a free digital preview of how the result will look, and the options with their prices.
A complete examination and a cone-beam scan of both jaws, to find what needs treating before anything else: gum disease, failing teeth, missing bone.
Shape, shade, proportion and bite settled for the whole mouth, and approved by you before any tooth is prepared.
Treatment in the sequence the plan sets, which can mean extractions and grafting before implants and crowns, with the lab in the building adjusting shade and fit.
Veneers with implants, from the gallery
Both arches rebuilt on implants · case 26

Rebuilding most or all of the teeth in both jaws to one plan, with crowns, bridges, veneers and implants as the case needs. Prosthodontists call it full-mouth rehabilitation, and it is the core of the specialty.
How is it different from a smile makeover?
A smile makeover works mostly on the teeth that show. A full-mouth reconstruction rebuilds the whole mouth, back teeth and bite included, often with implants where teeth are missing.

Usually people with several problems at once: worn or broken teeth, several missing teeth, gum disease or a bite that no longer meets evenly. The examination and scan decide whether the whole mouth needs rebuilding or only part of it.
It is done in stages, in the order the design requires. Where implants are part of it, allow anywhere from a few months to over a year, longer if bone has to be grafted first.
Can I see the result before treatment starts?
Yes. A digital preview of the finished smile is built from photos and scans of your mouth, free, and you approve the design before any tooth is prepared.
The price is set with the plan at the consultation. Most PPO dental plans are accepted, claims are filed for you, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.

props.text: Traditional dentures, snap-in dentures on implants, or fixed teeth that never come out: the ways to replace a full arch, compared by a prosthodontist, the dental specialist in replacing teeth.
A denture that fit last year can rub this year.

Without tooth roots to load it, the jawbone under a denture keeps receding, so the fit loosens. A loose denture rubs, needs adhesive, limits what you eat and has to be relined, and over years the bone loss changes the shape of the face.
Four ways to deal with dentures.
Acrylic teeth on a base that rests on the gums. The lowest cost, but they move, need relines and repairs, must come out to clean, and do nothing to stop bone loss.
A removable denture that clips onto two or more implants. It stops slipping, puts load back into the bone and still comes out for cleaning: around 60% of natural function at a moderate cost.
Teeth that never come out: a zirconia bridge screwed onto four to eight implants, often All-on-4 with provisional teeth the same day. Over 98% of natural function, at the highest cost.
A broken or damaged denture is one of the emergencies the practice makes room for, the same day wherever possible.
What dentures cost, counted over the years.
cost the least at the start. Over the years the relines, repairs and replacements add up, and the bone keeps receding because nothing loads it.
sit in the middle: the implants stop the movement and put load back into the bone, though the denture may still need the occasional reline.

costs the most up front and the least to keep: no relining, no adhesive, and it is cared for like natural teeth. The figure for your mouth is set at the consultation, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
Because the jawbone they rest on keeps receding once the teeth are gone, and nothing loads it. A reline refits the denture for a while; anchoring it to implants stops the movement.
Implant-supported dentures: a removable denture that clips onto two or more implants, so it stops slipping but still comes out for cleaning.
Can I go from dentures to fixed teeth?

Yes. Bone loss from years of wearing a denture often makes you a candidate for All-on-4 rather than ruling you out, and in most cases you leave the surgery wearing fixed provisional teeth. Some mouths need bone grafting first.

A prosthodontist: the dental specialist in replacing teeth, dentures included, with three years of training beyond dental school. Dr. Esam Nahlah is a board-certified prosthodontist and sees patients at both offices.
Call the office. A broken or damaged denture is treated as an emergency, and space is made to see you the same day wherever possible.
Most PPO dental plans are accepted, and the practice files the claims for you. What your plan covers is gone through at the consultation, along with the price and the financing.

props.text: Same-Day Dental Implants in McLean & Alexandria, VA

With All-on-4, most patients leave the surgery wearing a fixed provisional arch: four implants and a full set of teeth in a single visit. The final zirconia arch follows three to four months later. Planned and placed by board-certified prosthodontist Dr. Esam Nahlah.
Same-day teeth are real teeth, for now.

On implant day you receive a fully functional provisional arch in PMMA, fitted the day the implants go in and screwed down, not a removable denture. It carries you through the months while the implants fuse, and then it is replaced by the final arch in zirconia.
What happens on implant day, and in the months after.
An examination and a cone-beam scan show whether there is enough bone to load straight away. You leave knowing whether you qualify, what it costs and how long it takes.

Four implants placed through a printed guide, under local anesthetic with nitrous oxide or oral sedation, and the provisional arch fitted before you go home. After oral sedation, someone needs to drive you.
Three to four months while bone grows onto the implants: soft foods for those months, and reviews along the way to check integration and adjust the provisional.
The zirconia arch replaces the provisional, and two to four more months finish the healing around it. From then on it is brushed and flossed like natural teeth.
Who can have teeth the same day.
Same-day teeth need implants steady enough to carry a provisional arch on the day they go in. The cone-beam scan decides that at the consultation, and in most All-on-4 cases the answer is yes.
Patients whose remaining teeth are failing or already gone
Denture wearers tired of a plate that rubs and slips
People with bone loss: the rear implants tilt toward denser bone
Some cases need grafting first, which the scan shows at the consultation

Arches restored on implants at this practice.
Double arch means both jaws were restored on implants.
Can I really get teeth the same day as my implants?
With All-on-4, in most cases yes. You leave the same visit wearing a fixed provisional arch, and the final zirconia arch is fitted three to four months later.
Are same-day teeth my final teeth?
No. The same-day arch is a provisional in PMMA, fully functional and screwed in place, and it is adjusted at reviews while the implants fuse. The final arch is zirconia.
What can I eat with same-day teeth?
Soft foods for the next several months, while the implants integrate with the jawbone. That part is not optional, and it is the one people underestimate.
It is done under local anesthetic with nitrous oxide or oral sedation, so you stay relaxed throughout. Afterwards, patients generally report minor discomfort that over-the-counter medication handles.
What if I have bone loss?

Bone loss often makes you a candidate for All-on-4 rather than ruling you out, because the rear implants are angled toward denser bone. Some cases still need grafting first, and then the teeth wait for the bone to heal.
Can a single tooth be replaced the same day?
Sometimes. Where the case allows, the implant goes in at the time of the extraction, and qualifying patients leave with a temporary the same day. The scan shows whether yours qualifies.

props.text: Full-Mouth Dental Implants in McLean & Alexandria, VA

When most or all of your teeth are failing or gone, both arches can be rebuilt on implants: a fixed zirconia bridge on four to eight posts per arch, or a denture that clips onto them. Planned and placed by one board-certified prosthodontist, Dr. Esam Nahlah.
From surgery to the final zirconia

A full-mouth case is planned as one job rather than tooth by tooth. The cone-beam scan maps the bone in both jaws, and the upper and lower teeth are designed together so the bite balances. On this site these cases are called double arch.
Fixed teeth that stay in: screwed down, not taken out at night
Cared for like natural teeth, with six-monthly cleanings
Implants load the jawbone, which a denture resting on the gums cannot do
Zirconia, resistant to decay and to fractures and chips
Designed and milled in the practice's own laboratory
Three ways to replace every tooth.
Your scan, your bone and what you want from the result decide between them.
A removable denture on each arch, clipped onto two or more implants. Around 60% of natural function at a moderate cost, and it comes out for cleaning.
A fixed zirconia bridge on four implants per arch, the rear two tilted toward stronger bone. In most cases you leave surgery with fixed provisional teeth.
Where the bone and the bite call for it, each fixed arch is carried on up to eight implants. Over 98% of natural function, and the highest cost of the three.

What a full mouth costs, and how it is paid.

The number depends on how many implants each arch needs, whether extractions or grafting come first, and whether the teeth are a removable denture or fixed zirconia. It is set at your consultation, once the scan has been read; two quotes for the same mouth can differ by thousands for exactly those reasons.
Most PPO dental plans are accepted, and claims are filed for you. Financing reaches $60,000 with terms of up to 96 months, and a financial coordinator helps you apply.
Who is a candidate for full-mouth dental implants?

Adults whose teeth are mostly missing or failing, and people tired of loose dentures. Many already have enough bone; many of the rest qualify after bone grafting or extractions. The cone-beam scan at the consultation answers it for your mouth.
How many implants does a full mouth need?
Per arch: two or more for a removable implant denture, four for an All-on-4 fixed arch, and up to eight for a fixed bridge on more implants. The scan decides how many your bone will carry.
How long does full-mouth treatment take?

With All-on-4, about three to four months from surgery to the final zirconia arches, then a further two to four months for complete healing around them. Grafting, if you need it, adds several months of healing before the implants go in.
Will I have teeth while the implants heal?
Yes. With All-on-4, in most cases you leave the surgery wearing fixed provisional teeth, which stay in place while the implants fuse.
How do I look after full-mouth implants?
A fixed arch is brushed and flossed like natural teeth and stays in at night. The five-year warranty asks one thing of you: the six-monthly cleanings.
Is sedation available for full-mouth surgery?
Yes: nitrous oxide or oral sedation, given at the office by the practice's own team. The practice does not offer IV sedation or general anesthesia.
